notes:
SOURCE. Every IPA string is copied verbatim from the English Wiktionary entry named in sourceUrl. Bulk harvesting used the kaikki.org machine-readable extraction of English Wiktionary (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Vietnamese/kaikki.org-dictionary-Vietnamese.jsonl, downloaded 2026-09-07). Nothing here was transcribed by hand. All 281 sourceUrl pages were confirmed to exist via the MediaWiki API; 15 rows drawn at random across three seeded rounds were re-fetched from the live pages and their IPA matched byte-for-byte, as were both readings of the one multi-reading row.

DIALECT. HANOI / NORTHERN ONLY. Wiktionary gives Hà-Nội, Huế and Saigon transcriptions separately; only the row tagged Hà-Nội was taken, and the Huế and Saigon variants were discarded. Do not mix this file with a Southern reference.

TONE NOTATION — READ BEFORE SCORING. Tone is marked with CHAO TONE LETTERS at the end of each syllable, and Wiktionary's tone letters do NOT match Wikipedia's Help:IPA/Vietnamese for four of the six tones. Help:IPA/Vietnamese gives the Hanoi tones as ngang [˧], huyền [˨˩], sắc [˧˥], hỏi [˧˩], ngã [˧ˀ˥], nặng [˧ˀ˩]. This file, following Wiktionary, uses a doubled ˧˧ for ngang, ˧˦ (not ˧˥) for sắc, ˦ˀ˥ (not ˧ˀ˥) for ngã, and ˧˨ʔ (not ˧ˀ˩, and with a full glottal stop ʔ rather than the superscript ˀ) for nặng. Only huyền ˨˩ and hỏi ˧˩ agree. Both are attested descriptions of the same six tones and nothing here was converted between them; the file is internally consistent in Wiktionary's convention, which is what the scorer compares against. A scorer that hard-codes the Help:IPA values will mark every row wrong. All six tones occur in this file.

IPA CONVENTION. Wiktionary publishes these in square brackets (phonetic); the brackets were stripped and nothing else was altered. Syllables are separated by SPACES (not '.'), so a multi-syllable entry's IPA has as many space-separated groups as the orthography has syllables.

SYMBOL OUTLIERS. Two symbols used by Wiktionary's {{vi-pron}} module are not in the Help:IPA/Vietnamese table. 'ï' is the centralized allophone of /i/ before a velar-ish final, as in sinh [sïŋ˧˧] and tính [tïŋ˧˦]. 'ʊ' appears in the labialized velar codas after round vowels, as in hùng [hʊwŋ͡m˨˩]. The doubly-articulated codas ŋ͡m and k͡p, the unreleased-stop diacritic ̚, and the glottalization mark ˀ are all documented in Help:IPA/Vietnamese and appear as expected. These codas and the connected-syllable behaviour they encode are precisely what makes this tier worth evaluating.

ROMANIZATION. Set to null on every item. Vietnamese quốc ngữ is already Latin script, so there is no romanization step to evaluate; the orthography in 'text' is the romanization.

WORD TIER (181 items). Ranked by corpus frequency, not by hand: the OpenSubtitles-derived Vietnamese frequency list from hermitdave/FrequencyWords (https://github.com/hermitdave/FrequencyWords/blob/master/content/2018/vi/vi_50k.txt, CC BY-SA-4.0), which is well behaved for Vietnamese because the orthography puts spaces between syllables. The top 180 frequency-ranked entries surviving the filters below were kept. This list is cited as a source for Vietnamese frequency data by Wiktionary:Frequency_lists/Vietnamese. Wiktionary's Appendix:Vietnamese_Swadesh_list was used as a coverage cross-check.

MULTIPLE READINGS. Exactly one row needs this: 'ra', which is [zaː˧˧] as the verb 'to go out' but [ɹaː˧˧] as the noun 'bed sheet' (from French drap, which keeps its [ɹ] in the North). The second reading is in 'ipaAlternatives'. Because Vietnamese carries no romanization in this file, 'romanizationAlternatives' is null on that row, mirroring 'romanization'.

  Vietnamese needed almost nothing here, unlike Thai. Scanning the frequency list to rank 3000 turns up only 15 words with several Hanoi readings, and 14 of those are not genuine lexical ambiguity: they are single Latin letters transcribed as letter names (t, c, m, l, v, b, h, g, đ) or loanwords with a spelling pronunciation (video, pin, gen, game), plus 'chia' whose second reading is the letter spelling 'xi a'. Those were left out for the same reason Thai excludes initialism readings: crediting them would let a wrong transcription score as correct.

SENTENCE TIER (100 items). As with Thai, Wiktionary carries no IPA on usage examples, so the tier is drawn from headword entries with part of speech 'phrase', 'proverb' or 'intj' — everyday expressions and full-clause proverbs, each transcribed across the whole expression. Unlike Thai the supply here is NOT exhausted: roughly 340 further qualifying candidates of three syllables or more remain in the dump, so this tier can be extended without lowering the bar. Rows were chosen for everyday usefulness first, then well-known proverbs, and all are multi-word.

WHAT WAS EXCLUDED AND WHY. (1) Nothing is dropped for having several Hanoi readings any more; such a word carries them all in 'ipaAlternatives' (see MULTIPLE READINGS). (2) Entries with no Hà-Nội row at all (about 37% of the dump, mostly Han characters and rare or dialect-only terms). (3) Han/Nom character entries, romanization stubs, bound affixes and syllable-only entries. (4) Obsolete/archaic entries, alternative forms, nonstandard spellings, abbreviations. (5) Capitalized proper names in the word tier. (6) Vulgar and insult phrases (quỷ tha ma bắt, giấu như mèo giấu cứt, cái lồn gì thế, tiên sư, mẹ nó). (7) Political slogans whose inclusion in a shipped dataset would be a liability rather than a phonetics problem — 'từ sông ra biển' and its two alternative forms, 'vô sản toàn thế giới, đoàn kết lại', 'một quốc gia, hai chế độ'. (8) Near-duplicates of a row already present. (9) Word-tier items longer than two syllables, to keep that tier a word tier.
